{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal team  
**From:** In-house counsel (Customer)  
**Re:** Playbook review of Vendor's Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## 1. Executive summary

We have reviewed the Master Services Agreement against our playbook. The core risk-allocation provisions are strong and require no change: Vendor's indemnity package (§ 20.1–20.5), ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data (§ 14.1), the mutual liability cap at the greater of 12 months' Fees and USD 1,000,000 with our full Excluded Claims list (§ 21.1–21.3), assignment and change-of-control freedom (§ 24.1–24.4), licence scope including Affiliates and contractors (§ 13.1–13.3), warranties (§ 19.1–19.5), transition assistance and data return (§ 11.1–11.3), New York law and courts (§ 28.1), and Vendor insurance (§ 18.1–18.2).

Seven items require negotiation. Six of them are walk-away positions under the playbook: the full-term exclusivity obligation on us (§ 2.2), uncapped liquidated damages of USD 25,000 per day payable by us (§ 7.6), the absence of any Customer termination-for-convenience right in a three-year term (Section 9 / § 9.5), unlimited unannounced audits with remote access to our systems (§ 22.1), a Customer-side most-favoured-nation obligation (§ 7.2), and a 180-day non-renewal notice window that exceeds even our 90-day walk-away threshold (§ 8.2). The one-way 18-month non-solicit (§ 12.4) is a deviation we have narrowed to our fallback.

Notably, several of these provisions contradict terms Vendor has already accepted elsewhere in its own draft — § 2.2 conflicts with § 2.1 and § 12.3; § 7.2 conflicts with the no-most-favoured-customer acknowledgement in § 12.3; and § 22.1 conflicts with § 22.2, which already bars Vendor and its auditor from accessing our systems. That internal inconsistency should make these deletions and narrowings straightforward to land.

---

## 2. Findings table

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20.1 (with § 20.2–20.5) |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14.1 (with § 14.2–14.4, § 13.2, § 15.1) |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Compliant | § 21.1 (with § 21.2–21.3, § 1.5) |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with § 24.2–24.4, § 13.3) |
| 5 | High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 2.2 |
| 6 | High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.6 |
| 7 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (with § 13.2–13.4) |
| 8 | High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12.3 |
| 9 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | Section 9 (§ 9.1–9.3, § 9.5); term at § 8.1 |
| 10 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | § 22.1 (cf. § 22.2) |
| 11 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28.1 (with § 28.3) |
| 12 | Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.2 |
| 13 | Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments / volume restrictions | Compliant | § 2.1 (with § 12.3, § 7.1) |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 |
| 15 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | **Deviation** | § 8.2 (uplift cap at § 8.3) |
| 16 | Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11.1 (with § 11.2–11.3, § 10.1) |
| 17 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.1 (with § 19.2–19.5) |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18.1 (with § 18.2) |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

These are playbook walk-away positions. We should not sign without resolution.

### 3.1 Customer exclusivity — § 2.2 (High)
Section 2.2 makes Vendor our sole and exclusive provider of hosted analytics services for the full term, with no performance-based exit. Full-term exclusive dealing across an entire service category is our walk-away, and the clause contradicts § 2.1 (no purchase commitment) and § 12.3 (no exclusivity commitment).

> **[Playbook]** We have deleted the exclusivity obligation in 2.2. It conflicts with 2.1 and 12.3, which already confirm we have made no exclusivity or purchase commitment. If Vendor needs protection, our fallback is a narrowed service category, a 12-month duration, and an exit on service-level failure.

### 3.2 Liquidated damages payable by Customer — § 7.6 (High)
Section 7.6 imposes uncapped liquidated damages of USD 25,000 per day for any dependency delay, however minor. Accrual is unbounded and could exceed the remaining contract value.

> **[Playbook]** We have replaced the liquidated damages in 7.6 with schedule relief plus Vendor's documented, reasonable additional time-and-materials costs, and confirmed that no penalties are payable by us. Our playbook does not accept uncapped daily penalties on the Customer; a documented-cost remedy makes Vendor whole without unbounded exposure.

### 3.3 No Customer termination for convenience — Section 9 (High, missing)
Section 9 provides only termination for material breach (§ 9.1), insolvency (§ 9.2) and our special cause triggers (§ 9.3). There is no convenience right anywhere, against a three-year term (§ 8.1).

> **[Playbook]** We have inserted a new 9.6 giving us termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund keyed to Section 10.2, and confirming Vendor has no convenience right during a committed term. The absence of a Customer convenience right in a multi-year term is a walk-away for us.

### 3.4 Audit rights against Customer — § 22.1 (Medium)
Section 22.1 permits audits at any time without notice, including remote access to our systems and records. This directly contradicts § 22.2, which already provides that Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems.

> **[Playbook]** We have limited audits to once per 12 months, on 30 days' notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, records-based only and with no system access. This also resolves the conflict with 22.2. The cost allocation in 22.2 (Vendor pays unless underpayment exceeds 5%) already meets our position and is unchanged.

### 3.5 Customer-side MFN — § 7.2 (Medium)
Section 7.2 obliges us to offer Vendor terms no less favourable than the best terms we offer any other technology supplier — open-ended, with no product limit or comparison carve-outs. It also conflicts with the no-most-favoured-customer acknowledgement in § 12.3.

> **[Playbook]** We have deleted the MFN in 7.2. The obligation runs the wrong way and is inconsistent with 12.3, which records that we have given no most-favoured-customer commitment.

### 3.6 Non-renewal notice window — § 8.2 (Medium)
The 12-month renewal term and the § 8.3 uplift cap (lesser of CPI and 3%, 90 days' notice) meet our position. The 180-day opt-out window does not — it exceeds even our 90-day walk-away threshold.

> **[Playbook]** We have shortened the non-renewal notice in 8.2 from 180 days to 30 days and added a 60-day Vendor renewal reminder. Our fallback is 60 days. The renewal term and the 8.3 uplift cap are acceptable as drafted.

---

## 4. Other deviation to close

### Non-solicitation — § 12.4 (Medium)
The restraint binds only us, runs 18 months post-termination, covers any person employed by Vendor at any time during the term, bars "engaging" them (an effective no-hire), and has no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out.

> **[Playbook]** We have narrowed 12.4 to our fallback: mutual, 12 months from the end of a person's involvement, limited to involved personnel, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire element.

---

## 5. Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the seven open items — deletions at § 2.2 and § 7.2; replacement at § 7.6; new § 9.6; narrowing at § 22.1, § 12.4 and § 8.2 — with the playbook comments above.
2. **Flag the three internal inconsistencies** (§ 2.2 vs § 2.1/§ 12.3; § 7.2 vs § 12.3; § 22.1 vs § 22.2) in the cover note. These should be uncontroversial clean-ups rather than commercial concessions.
3. **Confirm walk-away escalation** with the business owner: § 2.2, § 7.6, the missing convenience right, § 22.1, § 7.2 and § 8.2 are not signable as drafted. Fallbacks are available on exclusivity (narrowed category / 12 months / service-level exit), audit, non-solicit and renewal notice (60 days).
4. **Take no action** on the compliant provisions (§ 20, § 14, § 21, § 24, § 13, § 12.3, § 28, § 2.1, § 11, § 19, § 18) and hold them as-is through negotiation.
5. **Order Form diligence:** § 2.1 confirms no minimum or take-or-pay commitment today. We will review each future Order Form to ensure no volume commitment is introduced at that level."}
